text_input: Patient is a 63-year-old female presenting with a one-month history of fever with chills, diffuse abdominal pain, and burning micturition for 15 days. She has a significant past history of alcoholic hepatitis and septic shock three months prior. Physical examination revealed an emaciated build, SpO2 of 92% on room air, and bilateral crepitations in the lungs. Investigations showed normocytic normochromic anemia, elevated HbA1c (7.0%), low serum iron (20.3 mcg/dL), and high ferritin (427 ng/mL). USG abdomen indicated chronic liver parenchymal disease (CLPD) with moderate ascites and small bowel thickening. 2D Echo showed normal LV systolic function (EF 55%) with diastolic dysfunction. Ascitic fluid analysis showed a SAAG of 0.9 and albumin of 1.3 g/dL. She was empirically started on Anti-Tubercular Treatment (ATT) for suspected abdominal tuberculosis and received antibiotics (Taxim, Metronidazole, Doxycycline) and blood transfusion.
